meta.description: The future official register of authorised banking and financial institutions: scope, data, search, state of authorisations and publication.

hero.title: The register of authorised institutions
hero.lead: The register is the official reference that will identify the institutions authorised to carry out a banking activity in Astoria. This page presents its role, content and publication principles.
hero.notice: No institution is published: the register will be opened with the official data.

comprendre.title: Understanding the register
comprendre.lead: The register of authorised institutions will be the official list of institutions authorised to carry out a banking activity.

paragraphs.p1: The register lists the authorised institutions, with the essential information on each: name, status, category, licence, authorised activities and state of the authorisation. It will be kept and published by the Central Bank.
paragraphs.p2: Its purpose is twofold: to enable the public to identify authorised institutions, and to enable everyone to check the situation of an institution before entering into a relationship.

public.title: A public register
public.text: An official, open list available to all.

verification.title: Check
verification.text: Check that an institution is indeed authorised.

confiance.title: Confidence
confiance.text: The guarantee of dealing with authorised institutions.

actualite.title: Up to date
actualite.text: A register kept up to date with the situation of each.

perimetre.title: The scope of the register
perimetre.lead: The register covers all institutions subject to authorisation under Astorian law.

paragraphs.p1: It will include institutions authorised to carry out a banking activity, specialised institutions, payment institutions and other institutions subject to approval or authorisation.
paragraphs.p2: The exact categories will be those provided for by Astorian law. The register will rely on the categories presented in the Banks theme.

bullets.b1: Institutions authorised to carry out a banking activity.
bullets.b2: Specialised institutions and payment institutions.
bullets.b3: Other institutions subject to approval or authorisation.

perimetre.notice: The definitive scope will be the one set by the official regulatory framework.

recherche.title: Search for an institution
recherche.lead: The register will make it possible to search for an institution according to several criteria.

paragraphs.p1: The search can be done by name, by category, by status or by type of licence. The results will present the essential information on each institution.

links.statut: Filter by status of the authorisation

donnees.title: The data of the register
donnees.lead: Each entry in the register will include a standard set of information.

paragraphs.p1: This information will make it possible to identify each institution precisely and to know the exact state of its authorisation.

nom.label: Name
nom.value: The corporate name of the institution.

date.label: Date
date.value: The date of authorisation or amendment.

activites.title: Authorised activities
activites.lead: The register will specify the activities that each institution is authorised to carry out.

paragraphs.p1: The scope of activity depends on the category of the institution and the terms of its authorisation. Not all activities are authorised for all institutions.
paragraphs.p2: The register will indicate, for each institution, the activities actually authorised.

activites.notice: Activities will be specified according to the terms of each authorisation.

etat.title: State of the authorisation
etat.lead: The register will report on the situation of each authorisation.

paragraphs.p1: Each entry will include the state of the authorisation: active, suspended, restricted or withdrawn, as well as the corresponding dates and decisions.

table.caption: Possible states of an authorisation

0.2: The institution carries out its activities.

2.2: The institution can no longer operate.

table.note: The exact terminology of the states will be that of the official regulatory framework.

verifier.title: Check a licence
verifier.lead: Before entering into a relationship, it is prudent to check the situation of an institution.

paragraphs.p1: Identify the institution, consult its file, check its licence and the state of its authorisation. This information will be available in the register.

consulter.title: Consult
consulter.text: Consult its file in the register.

verifier.title: Check
verifier.text: Check the licence and authorised activities.

obtenir.title: Confirm
obtenir.text: Confirm the state of the authorisation.

publication.title: The publication of the register
publication.lead: The register will be published as soon as the official data are available.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank will publish the register, keep the entries up to date and make changes of status public in accordance with the applicable rules.

publication.notice: No substitute data will be presented as official before the publication of the register.

meta.title: The categories of institutions
meta.description: The different categories of institutions in the Astorian banking system: commercial banks, public banks, specialised and payment institutions.

hero.title: The categories of institutions
hero.lead: The Astorian banking system is made up of several categories of institutions, each authorised to carry out specific activities.
hero.notice: The categories are presented as institutional categories; the definitive legal classification will be the one provided for by Astorian law.

comprendre.title: Understanding the categories
comprendre.lead: The category of an institution determines the scope of the activities it can carry out.

paragraphs.p1: The classification of institutions serves a twofold need: to govern the activity of each and to inform the public about the nature of the institutions.
paragraphs.p2: Each category is associated with a status, authorised activities and obligations. These elements are specified by the authorisation.

classification.title: Classification
classification.text: Categories defined by the nature of the activity.

activites.title: Activities
activites.text: Each category carries out a specific scope.

statut.title: Status
statut.text: A legal status specific to each category.

commerciales.title: Commercial banks
commerciales.lead: Commercial banks serve individuals, businesses and local authorities.

paragraphs.p1: They offer the full range of banking services: accounts, deposits, credit, payments, savings and financing.
paragraphs.p2: They are the institutions with the most direct contact with the public.

publiques.title: Public banks
publiques.lead: Public banks carry out public-interest missions.

paragraphs.p1: They operate in areas where public intervention responds to a collective need: financing local authorities, supporting strategic sectors or facilitating access to banking services.
paragraphs.p2: Their activity takes place within a specific legal framework and governance.

specialisees.title: Specialised institutions
specialisees.lead: Specialised institutions operate on a specific segment of financing.

paragraphs.p1: Their activity focuses on one field: financing real estate, trade, equipment, or managing savings.
paragraphs.p2: Their scope of activity is narrower than that of commercial banks.

epargne.title: Savings
epargne.text: Collecting savings within a defined framework.

paiement.title: Payment institutions
paiement.lead: Payment institutions offer payment services without taking deposits.

paragraphs.p1: They execute payment transactions on behalf of their customers: transfers, card payments, direct debits.
paragraphs.p2: They are subject to a specific authorisation, distinct from the banking authorisation, and to obligations adapted to their activity.

bullets.b1: Executing payment transactions on behalf of customers.
bullets.b2: A specific authorisation for payment services.
bullets.b3: Obligations to protect customers' funds.

autres.title: The other categories
autres.lead: Other categories of institutions may be provided for by Astorian law.

paragraphs.p1: Depending on changes to the legal framework, other categories of institutions may be authorised to carry out specific financial activities.
paragraphs.p2: These categories will be presented as soon as they are defined by the regulatory framework.

bullets.b1: Institutions specialised in particular financial services.
bullets.b2: Categories created by Astorian law.
bullets.b3: Changes to the classification over time.

autres.notice: Additional categories will be presented as soon as they are officially defined.

regime.title: The applicable regime
regime.lead: The applicable regime depends on the category of the institution.

paragraphs.p1: Status, authorised activities, prudential requirements and obligations vary by category.

table.caption: Overview of regimes by category
table.note: The detailed regime will be the one set by the official regulatory framework.

evolution.title: The evolution of categories
evolution.lead: The classification of institutions can evolve with the law.

paragraphs.p1: The categories of institutions evolve with the legal framework and the needs of the economy.

evolution.notice: Changes to the classification will be presented as soon as they are officially published.

meta.title: The institutions' accounts
meta.description: The accounts held by credit institutions with the Central Bank: nature, use, required reserves, refinancing and payment systems.

hero.title: The institutions' accounts
hero.lead: Credit institutions hold an account with the Central Bank. This account is the vehicle for liquidity, reserves and interbank payments.
hero.notice: The operational conditions of the accounts will be specified by the applicable framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding the accounts
comprendre.lead: The account held with the Central Bank is a central instrument of the banking system.

paragraphs.p1: Each credit institution holds an account with the Central Bank. This account records the movements between the institution and the central bank, as well as interbank settlements.
paragraphs.p2: It is the instrument through which the institution accesses liquidity, holds its reserves and settles its operations.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: An account held by each institution with the BCA.

condition.title: Conditions
condition.text: Conditions set by the applicable framework.

nature.title: The nature of the account
nature.lead: The Central Bank account has specific characteristics.

paragraphs.p1: The account held with the Central Bank differs from customer accounts: it is held by the institution itself and serves institutional purposes.
paragraphs.p2: Its balance represents the position of the institution vis-à-vis the central bank.

type.label: Type
type.value: An institutional account of the institution.

solde.label: Balance
solde.value: The position of the institution with the BCA.

utilisation.title: The use of the account
utilisation.lead: The account serves several institutional purposes.

paragraphs.p1: It allows liquidity to be held, interbank settlements to be executed, reserves to be satisfied and the data needed by the central bank to be transmitted.

reporting.title: Reporting
reporting.text: Data transmitted to the central bank.

reserves.title: Required reserves
reserves.lead: Institutions hold reserves with the Central Bank.

paragraphs.p1: The required reserve regime requires institutions to hold a certain amount of reserves with the Central Bank, based on their deposits.
paragraphs.p2: These reserves contribute to controlling bank liquidity and to implementing monetary policy.

reserves.notice: The exact arrangements of the reserve regime will be those set by the applicable framework.

refinancement.title: Refinancing
refinancement.lead: The account is the vehicle for the central bank's refinancing operations.

paragraphs.p1: Institutions can obtain liquidity from the Central Bank through refinancing operations.
paragraphs.p2: These operations rely on the institution's account and are governed by the conditions set by the central bank.

conditions.title: Conditions
conditions.text: Conditions defined by the central bank.

systeme.title: Payment systems
systeme.lead: The account participates in the functioning of payment systems.

paragraphs.p1: Interbank settlements are executed on accounts held with the Central Bank, within the payment systems.

obligations.title: Institutional obligations
obligations.lead: Holding an account with the Central Bank comes with obligations.

paragraphs.p1: Institutions must comply with the conditions of access, maintain their reserves and transmit the information required by the central bank.
paragraphs.p2: These obligations ensure the orderly functioning of the monetary system.

bullets.b1: Compliance with the conditions of access to the account.
bullets.b2: Holding the required reserves.
bullets.b3: Transmitting data to the central bank.

orienter.title: Go further
orienter.lead: These subjects are explored in the dedicated themes and pages.

meta.title: Complaints
meta.description: How to complain to a banking institution: before complaining, the procedure, mediation, handling standards and the role of the institution.

hero.title: Complaints
hero.lead: Every customer of a banking institution has the right to complain in case of difficulty. This page explains how to exercise this right and how complaints are handled.
hero.notice: The practical arrangements for complaints will be specified by the applicable framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding complaints
comprendre.lead: The complaint is the right recognised to any customer to contest a situation.

paragraphs.p1: A complaint is a request by which a customer contests a situation: an operation, fees, a decision or a service of their institution.
paragraphs.p2: Any institution is required to handle complaints under defined conditions, to respond within the deadlines and to inform the customer of their remedies.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: A request for contestation by the customer.

droit.title: The right
droit.text: A right recognised to any customer.

suivi.title: Follow-up
suivi.text: Tracking of complaints by the institution.

avant.title: Before complaining
avant.lead: A few precautions before lodging a complaint.

paragraphs.p1: Before complaining, it is useful to gather the elements of the situation: contracts, statements, correspondence.
paragraphs.p2: It is also advisable to first contact the department of the institution concerned.

bullets.b1: Gather the documents and evidence.
bullets.b2: Re-read the terms of the contract and the conditions.
bullets.b3: Respect the complaint deadlines.
bullets.b5: Keep a record of the exchanges.

procedure.title: The complaint procedure
procedure.lead: The complaint follows a process in several stages.

paragraphs.p1: The typical process includes the request to the institution, written acknowledgement, handling, response and, in case of disagreement, the remedies.

etablissement.title: Contact the institution
etablissement.text: Lodge the complaint with the institution.

ecrit.title: Written acknowledgement
ecrit.text: The institution acknowledges receipt of the complaint.

traitement.title: Handling
traitement.text: The complaint is examined within the deadlines.

reponse.title: Response
reponse.text: The institution responds to the customer.

recours.title: Remedies
recours.text: In case of disagreement, remedies are possible.

mediation.title: Mediation
mediation.lead: In case of persistent disagreement, mediation may be proposed.

paragraphs.p1: Mediation is an amicable way of resolving disputes, distinct from the judicial route.
paragraphs.p2: It is generally open after an unsatisfactory response from the institution.

condition.label: Condition
condition.value: A prior complaint handled by the institution.

procedure.label: Procedure
procedure.value: A procedure distinct from the judicial route.

normes.title: Handling standards
normes.lead: The handling of complaints follows standards.

paragraphs.p1: These standards relate to acknowledgement of receipt, deadlines, the reasoned response and the information provided to the customer.

table.caption: Overview of handling standards

3.1: Inform the customer of their remedies.

table.note: The detailed standards will be those set by the regulatory framework.

etablissement.title: The role of the institution
etablissement.lead: The institution is the customer's first point of contact.

paragraphs.p1: It must organise the handling of complaints, designate the responsible persons and ensure follow-up.
paragraphs.p2: It must also inform the customer of the progress of their complaint.

bullets.b1: Receive complaints from customers.
bullets.b2: Acknowledge receipt and inform the customer.
bullets.b3: Handle the complaint within the deadlines.
bullets.b5: Inform the customer of the remedies available.

guides.title: Guides and resources
guides.lead: Additional resources for understanding the applicable framework.

paragraphs.p1: The information for institutions and the division of responsibilities complete this page.

links.roleBca: The role of the Central Bank

orientation.title: Orientations

paragraphs.p1: Consult the register to identify an institution and its contact details.

orientation.notice: Official contacts will be published in the register of institutions.

meta.title: The conditions of authorisation
meta.description: The conditions required to obtain a banking authorisation: capital, governance, systems, risk management, business model and ownership.

hero.title: The conditions of authorisation
hero.lead: Granting a banking authorisation is subject to precise conditions, which guarantee the soundness and regularity of the project.
hero.notice: The detailed conditions will be those set by the official regulatory framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding the conditions
comprendre.lead: The conditions of authorisation are the requirements that an applicant must fulfil.

paragraphs.p1: They relate to capital, governance, officers, ownership, information systems, security, risk management, continuity and compliance.
paragraphs.p2: They guarantee that the institution will be able to carry out its activity safely and in an orderly manner.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: The requirements to be met to be authorised.

principe.title: Principle
principe.text: Guarantee the soundness of the banking project.

controle.title: Control
controle.text: An assessment on a case-by-case basis.

capital.title: Capital requirements
capital.lead: The applicant must have sufficient capital.

paragraphs.p1: The capital must be sufficient in relation to the project, its risks and its volume of activity.
paragraphs.p2: Its origin must be clear and its availability guaranteed.

bullets.b1: Capital at least equal to the minimum provided for.
bullets.b2: Capital sufficient in relation to the project.
bullets.b3: A clear and documented origin.
bullets.b4: The effective availability of the capital.

capital.notice: The minimum amount of capital will be set by the regulatory framework.

gouvernance.title: Governance and organisation
gouvernance.lead: Governance must be suited to the project.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant must present a clear organisation, defined bodies and robust decision-making procedures.

bullets.b1: Defined management and control bodies.
bullets.b2: Competent and reputable officers.
bullets.b3: The independence of control functions.

systemes.title: IT systems
systemes.lead: Information systems must be reliable and secure.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant must have systems suited to its activity, secure and available.
paragraphs.p2: It must also provide for data backup and the traceability of operations.

bullets.b1: Systems protected against unauthorised access.
bullets.b2: Available and high-performing systems.
bullets.b3: Regular data backups.

risques.title: Risk management
risques.lead: Risk management must be proportionate to the project.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant must identify, measure and control the main risks of its activity.

model.title: The business model
model.lead: The project must rest on a viable business model.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant must present its business model: activities envisaged, sources of income, profitability and outlook.
paragraphs.p2: The model must be coherent with the project and the means of the institution.

bullets.b1: A clear description of the activities envisaged.
bullets.b2: Credible forecast profitability.
bullets.b3: A coherent development strategy.

actionnariat.title: Ownership and control
actionnariat.lead: Ownership must be transparent and suitable.

paragraphs.p1: The identity and quality of the shareholders are examined, in order to guarantee the regularity of the control of the institution.
paragraphs.p2: Safeguards are provided to prevent inappropriate use of control.

bullets.b1: Clear and identifiable ownership.
bullets.b2: Suitable shareholders in relation to the project.
bullets.b3: Safeguards against conflicts of interest.

actionnariat.notice: The ownership transparency rules will be those of the regulatory framework.

approfondir.title: Go further
approfondir.lead: The conditions are part of the authorisation process.

paragraphs.p1: The complete process, from setting up the file to the decision, is presented in the dedicated page.

meta.title: Submitting an authorisation application
meta.description: The authorisation application process: project, file, processing, assessment, decision, after the decision and cases of refusal.

hero.title: Submitting an authorisation application
hero.lead: The authorisation application follows a predictable process, from setting up the project to entering the register. This page details each stage.
hero.notice: A future operational platform will make it possible to actually submit a file. This page describes the process.

comprendre.title: Understanding the process
comprendre.lead: The authorisation application is a regulated and documented process.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant sets up a project, submits a file, follows the processing, and receives a decision.
paragraphs.p2: In the event of authorisation, the institution is entered in the register and subject to the applicable obligations.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: The procedure for obtaining the authorisation.

parcours.title: The application process
parcours.lead: The process takes place in several stages.

paragraphs.p1: Each stage is documented and concludes with a decision or a next stage.

projet.title: The banking project
projet.lead: The project forms the basis of the application.

paragraphs.p1: The applicant presents its project: activities, market, governance, risks and finances.
paragraphs.p2: The project must be coherent, documented and viable.

bullets.b1: The activities envisaged.
bullets.b2: The market and customers targeted.
bullets.b3: Governance and organisation.

dossier.title: The application file
dossier.lead: The file brings together the supporting documents.

paragraphs.p1: The file includes the documents relating to the applicant, the project, governance, capital and systems.
paragraphs.p2: It must be complete to allow processing.

table.caption: Overview of the contents of the file

1.1: The description of the project and activities.

table.note: The exact contents of the file will be set by the regulatory framework.

instruction.title: Processing
instruction.lead: Processing is the phase of examining the file.

paragraphs.p1: The competent authority verifies the completeness of the file, analyses the project and exchanges with the applicant.
paragraphs.p2: It may request additions or clarifications.

reception.title: Receipt
reception.text: The file is submitted and registered.

completude.title: Completeness
completude.text: The completeness of the file is verified.

analyse.title: Analysis
analyse.text: The project and the conditions are analysed.

echange.title: Exchanges
echange.text: Exchanges are conducted with the applicant.

paragraphs.p1: The decision is taken by the competent authority on the basis of the file and the conditions of authorisation.
paragraphs.p2: It is notified to the applicant with its reasons.

autorite.label: Authority
autorite.value: The competent authority according to the mandates.

apres.title: After the decision
apres.lead: The granting of the authorisation opens the life of the institution.

paragraphs.p1: The authorised institution is entered in the register and subject to the applicable obligations.

registre.title: Register
registre.text: The entry in the register is made.

refus.title: In case of refusal

paragraphs.p1: In case of refusal, the applicant is informed of the reasons for the decision.
paragraphs.p2: It may present a modified project or, where applicable, exercise the remedies provided for.

bullets.b1: A reasoned decision.
bullets.b2: The possible remedies.
bullets.b3: The possibility of presenting a different project.
bullets.b4: The possibility of renewing the application.

refus.notice: The remedies will be those provided for by Astorian law.

meta.title: Banking licences
meta.description: The different types of licences in the Astorian banking system: banking licence, specialised licence, payment authorisation and other authorisations.

hero.title: Banking licences
hero.lead: Licences define the level and scope of authorisations. This page presents the different types of licences in the Astorian system.
hero.notice: The licences are presented as institutional categories; the precise catalogue will be that of the official regulatory framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding licences
comprendre.lead: A licence is the authorisation to carry out a set of activities.

paragraphs.p1: The licence determines the level of authorisation of the institution and the scope of its activities.
paragraphs.p2: The system has several levels, from banking operations to payment services.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: The authorisation to carry out defined activities.

importance.title: Importance
importance.text: The level of authorisation of the institution.

controle.title: Control
controle.text: Compliance with the conditions is controlled.

bancaire.title: The banking licence
bancaire.lead: The banking licence is the most extensive authorisation.

paragraphs.p1: It authorises the exercise of banking operations: taking deposits, extending credit and payment services.
paragraphs.p2: It is accompanied by the most complete requirements.

definition.label: Definition
definition.value: The authorisation to carry out banking operations.

specialisee.title: The specialised licence
specialisee.lead: The specialised licence governs a particular field of financing.

paragraphs.p1: It authorises the exercise of activities limited to one field or to one type of operation.
paragraphs.p2: Its scope is narrower than that of the banking licence.

definition.label: Definition
definition.value: An authorisation limited to one field.

paiement.title: The payment authorisation
paiement.lead: The payment authorisation covers payment services.

paragraphs.p1: It makes it possible to carry out payment services without taking deposits.
paragraphs.p2: It is accompanied by conditions adapted to the payment activity.

autres.title: The other authorisations
autres.lead: Other authorisations may be provided for by Astorian law.

paragraphs.p1: They concern particular financial activities: savings, transfer, management or advice.
paragraphs.p2: Each is defined and governed by the regulatory framework.

autres.notice: These authorisations will be presented as soon as they are officially defined.

evolution.title: The evolution of licences
evolution.lead: A licence can evolve during the life of the institution.

paragraphs.p1: Extension, amendment, suspension or withdrawal: the licence evolves according to the situation of the institution.

bullets.b1: The extension of the scope of activity.
bullets.b2: The amendment of the conditions.
bullets.b3: Temporary suspension.

tableau.title: Compare the types of licences
tableau.lead: A comparative overview of the main types of licences.

paragraphs.p1: This table summarises the characteristics of the main types of licences.

table.caption: Comparison of the types of licences
table.note: The official catalogue of licences will be that of the regulatory framework.

consulter.title: Consult the information
consulter.lead: Check the licences and the applicable conditions.

paragraphs.p1: The register will make it possible to check the licence of an institution and the conditions of obtaining it.

meta.title: The withdrawal of the authorisation
meta.description: The withdrawal of the banking authorisation: definition, grounds, suspension, procedure, consequences, voluntary renunciation and customer protection.

hero.title: The withdrawal of the authorisation
hero.lead: An authorisation can be withdrawn in defined circumstances. This page explains the grounds, the procedure and the consequences of the withdrawal.
hero.notice: The detailed rules of the withdrawal will be those set by the official regulatory framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding the withdrawal
comprendre.lead: The withdrawal of the authorisation is the decision that brings an authorisation to an end.

paragraphs.p1: The withdrawal of the authorisation is a serious measure, taken under defined conditions, which brings the authorisation to exercise to an end.
paragraphs.p2: It fits into a protective framework: the procedure, the grounds and the consequences are regulated.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: The end of the authorisation to operate.

motifs.title: The grounds for withdrawal
motifs.lead: Withdrawal may be decided for defined grounds.

paragraphs.p1: The grounds concern situations where the institution no longer meets the conditions or can no longer carry out its activity.
paragraphs.p2: The exact grounds will be those provided for by Astorian law.

bullets.b1: Failure to comply with the conditions of authorisation.
bullets.b2: Cessation of activity.
bullets.b3: Serious breaches of obligations.
bullets.b4: The loss of the required conditions.
bullets.b5: The grounds provided for by law.

suspension.title: The suspension
suspension.lead: The suspension is distinct from the withdrawal.

paragraphs.p1: The suspension temporarily interrupts the exercise of the activity, without bringing the authorisation to an end.
paragraphs.p2: It may be pronounced under defined conditions.

definition.label: Definition
definition.value: The temporary interruption of the activity.

effets.label: Effects
effets.value: The temporary halt of the exercise.

suspension.notice: The conditions of the suspension will be those set by the regulatory framework.

procedure.title: The procedure
procedure.lead: The withdrawal follows a regulated procedure.

paragraphs.p1: The procedure includes the alert, the formal notice, the decision, the notification and the publication.

alerte.title: Alert
alerte.text: The institution is alerted to the situation.

consequences.title: The consequences for the institution
consequences.lead: The withdrawal has consequences for the institution.

paragraphs.p1: The institution ceases its activity, organises the closure of its operations and informs its customers.
paragraphs.p2: The liquidation arrangements are regulated.

bullets.b1: The cessation of the authorised activity.
bullets.b2: The orderly closure of operations.
bullets.b3: The information and protection of customers.
bullets.b5: Liquidation according to the arrangements provided for.

volontaire.title: Voluntary renunciation
volontaire.lead: An institution may voluntarily renounce its authorisation.

paragraphs.p1: The institution may voluntarily cease its activity and renounce its authorisation.
paragraphs.p2: This renunciation follows a distinct procedure.

bullets.b1: The decision to renounce.
bullets.b2: The relinquishment of the authorisation.
bullets.b3: The closure of operations.

protection.title: Customer protection
protection.lead: Customer protection is central in the event of withdrawal.

paragraphs.p1: Customers must be informed and their funds protected.
paragraphs.p2: The account closure arrangements are regulated.

devoirs.label: Duties
devoirs.value: The information and protection of customers.

consulter.title: Consult the register
consulter.lead: The register reports on the situation of authorisations.

paragraphs.p1: The register of institutions will make it possible to check the state of authorisations.

meta.title: The applicable texts
meta.description: The documentary library of banking regulation: regulations, decisions, instructions, frameworks, guides and technical documents.

hero.title: The applicable texts
hero.lead: The regulatory framework is made up of several types of texts. This page presents this documentary library and its organisation.
hero.notice: No document is published on this page until the official texts are available.

comprendre.title: Understanding the texts
comprendre.lead: The applicable texts constitute the documentary basis of the regulation.

paragraphs.p1: The regulatory framework is made up of texts of different natures: regulations, decisions, instructions, frameworks and guides.
paragraphs.p2: Each type of text has its own scope and function.

paragraphs.p1: Regulations set general rules applicable to all institutions.
paragraphs.p2: They form the foundation of the regulatory framework.

effet.label: Effect
effet.value: They set the rules of the framework.

decisions.title: The decisions
decisions.lead: Decisions have an individual or categorical scope.

paragraphs.p1: Decisions apply to one institution or to a category of institutions.
paragraphs.p2: They may specify or complement the general rules.

hero.title: Prudential standards
hero.lead: Prudential standards set a common baseline of soundness for institutions. This page presents the main families of requirements, without publishing undefined ratios.
hero.notice: No quantified ratio or threshold is published at this stage; official values will be specified by the regulatory framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding the standards
comprendre.lead: Prudential standards aim at the soundness and resilience of institutions.

paragraphs.p1: Prudential standards are the requirements that ensure that an institution has sufficient resources to absorb its losses and meet its obligations.
paragraphs.p2: They cover capital, liquidity, solvency, exposures and loss-absorption capacity.

objectif.title: Objective
objectif.text: Guarantee the resilience of the system.

fondsPropres.title: Capital
fondsPropres.lead: Capital is the first line of protection.

paragraphs.p1: Capital is the resources that the institution can mobilise to absorb its losses.
paragraphs.p2: It is made up of different categories of resources and must reach a defined level.

niveau.label: Level
niveau.value: A level defined by the framework.

fondsPropres.notice: The minimum level of capital will be set by the regulatory framework.

liquidite.title: Liquidity requirements
liquidite.lead: Liquidity requirements guarantee the ability to meet obligations.

paragraphs.p1: Liquidity is the ability of an institution to meet its short-term obligations.
paragraphs.p2: The liquidity requirements provide for ratios and reference horizons.

solvabilite.title: Solvency ratios
solvabilite.lead: Solvency measures the ability to absorb losses.

paragraphs.p1: Solvency ratios relate capital to the risks taken by the institution.

solvabilite.notice: The ratio levels will be set by the official regulatory framework.

exposition.title: Exposures and concentrations
exposition.lead: The standards govern exposures and risk concentrations.

paragraphs.p1: An institution must measure and limit its exposures, in particular to large counterparties, and avoid excessive concentrations.
paragraphs.p2: Limits are provided to control these risks.

bullets.b1: Governing exposures to counterparties.
bullets.b2: Limiting risk concentrations.
bullets.b3: Taking into account groups of counterparties.

absorption.title: Loss-absorption capacity
absorption.lead: Loss-absorption capacity is a central objective.

paragraphs.p1: The institution must have resources enabling it to absorb its losses without compromising its stability.
paragraphs.p2: Specific instruments may be provided for this purpose.

paragraphs.p1: The standards are analysed, subject to consultation, published and then applied according to a calendar.
paragraphs.p2: This approach guarantees the legibility and predictability of the requirements.

analyse.title: Analysis
analyse.text: The analysis of risks and needs.

comprendre.lead: This page is intended for institutions and their teams.

paragraphs.p1: It brings together the regulatory obligations, references and resources useful for carrying out the banking activity.
paragraphs.p2: It is intended to be updated as the framework evolves.

obligations.title: Regulatory obligations
obligations.lead: Institutions are subject to several families of obligations.

paragraphs.p1: These obligations relate to reporting, prudential requirements, compliance, governance and security.
paragraphs.p2: They are proportionate to the activity of each institution.

securite.title: Security and continuity
securite.lead: Security and continuity are essential obligations.

paragraphs.p1: Institutions must ensure cybersecurity, business continuity and recovery after an incident.
paragraphs.p2: They must also manage incidents and regularly test their arrangements.

hero.lead: The Financial Supervisory Authority (AMSF) is the independent authority responsible for financial supervision and regulation. This page presents its responsibilities and its separation from the Central Bank.
hero.notice: The detailed responsibilities of the AMSF are those provided for by Astorian law.

comprendre.title: Understanding the AMSF
comprendre.lead: The AMSF is the financial supervision and regulation authority within its independent mandate.

paragraphs.p1: The Financial Supervisory Authority (AMSF) is an independent authority responsible for supervising financial institutions and markets.
paragraphs.p2: It exercises a regulation and supervision mandate, distinct from that of the Central Bank.
paragraphs.p3: This separation guarantees the independence of supervision and the clarity of responsibilities.

difference.title: Distinction
difference.text: An authority distinct from the BCA.

comprendre.notice: The exact scope of the responsibilities is the one provided for by Astorian law.

separation.title: The BCA - AMSF separation
separation.lead: The Astorian model separates the mandates of the Central Bank and of the AMSF.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank acts on money, liquidity and infrastructures. The AMSF supervises and regulates financial institutions and markets.
paragraphs.p2: The two institutions cooperate on shared matters, each within its scope.

bca.label: BCA

perimetre.title: The scope of responsibility
perimetre.lead: The AMSF operates across a broad financial scope.

paragraphs.p1: Its responsibilities cover regulation, supervision, controls, sanctions and customer protection.

hero.lead: The Central Bank of Astoria acts on money, liquidity and infrastructures, and contributes to financial stability within the framework of its mandate.
hero.notice: The role of the Central Bank is presented within the framework of its mandate; financial supervision falls within the AMSF's mandate.

comprendre.title: Understanding the role of the BCA
comprendre.lead: The Central Bank exercises specific responsibilities in the banking system.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank of Astoria is responsible for money, liquidity and payment infrastructures.
paragraphs.p2: It contributes to the stability of the financial system within the framework of its mandate.
paragraphs.p3: It is not the financial supervisory authority: this mission falls within the AMSF's mandate.

monetaire.title: Monetary stability
monetaire.lead: Monetary stability is a central mission of the Central Bank.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank conducts monetary policy and ensures the stability of the currency.
paragraphs.p2: This mission is distinct from the supervision of institutions.

liquidite.title: Liquidity
liquidite.lead: The Central Bank provides liquidity to the banking system.

paragraphs.p1: It conducts operations, manages reserves, refinances institutions and offers standing facilities.
paragraphs.p2: These interventions aim at the orderly functioning of the money market.

bullets.b3: The refinancing of institutions.

infrastructures.title: The infrastructures
infrastructures.lead: The Central Bank contributes to payment and settlement infrastructures.

paragraphs.p1: It ensures the proper functioning of the infrastructures that ensure the circulation of money and the settlement of operations.
paragraphs.p2: These infrastructures are essential to the stability of the system.

bullets.b1: Payment systems.
bullets.b2: Settlement systems.
bullets.b3: The security and resilience of infrastructures.

acces.title: Access to operations
acces.lead: Access to central bank operations is regulated.

paragraphs.p1: Authorised institutions can access the Central Bank's operations under defined conditions.
paragraphs.p2: This access relies on the accounts held with the Central Bank.

systemique.title: Systemic risks
systemique.lead: The Central Bank monitors systemic risks falling within its mandate.

paragraphs.p1: It detects fragilities, coordinates its action, prevents risks and manages situations of stress.
paragraphs.p2: This action takes place within the framework of its mandate and in cooperation with the other authorities.

surveillance.title: Surveillance
surveillance.lead: The Central Bank carries out surveillance within the framework of its responsibilities.

paragraphs.p1: It monitors indicators, supervises infrastructures and analyses data falling within its mandate.
paragraphs.p2: This surveillance is not to be confused with the AMSF's financial supervision.

bullets.b2: Monitoring indicators.
bullets.b3: The surveillance of infrastructures.

frontieres.title: The boundaries with the AMSF
frontieres.lead: The role of the Central Bank is distinct from that of the AMSF.

paragraphs.p1: The Central Bank acts on money, liquidity and infrastructures; the AMSF supervises and regulates institutions and markets.
paragraphs.p2: The two institutions cooperate while respecting their respective scopes.

frontieres.notice: The detailed division of responsibilities is presented in the dedicated pages.

hero.title: Controls and inspections
hero.lead: Supervision relies on off-site and on-site controls, as well as inspections. This page explains how they are conducted.
hero.notice: The detailed arrangements for the controls will be specified by the official regulatory framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding the controls
comprendre.lead: Controls verify the compliance and soundness of institutions.

paragraphs.p1: Controls and inspections make it possible to verify the compliance of institutions, detect fragilities and prevent risks.
paragraphs.p2: They rely on data, documents and on-site visits.

controles.title: The types of controls
controles.lead: Several types of controls are conducted.

paragraphs.p1: Controls can be documentary, on-site, thematic or definitive.

documentaire.title: Documentary
documentaire.text: The examination of documents and data.

thematique.title: Thematic
thematique.text: A control targeted on a subject.

donnees.title: Data and indicators
donnees.lead: Controls rely on data and indicators.

paragraphs.p1: Institutions transmit data, the authorities monitor indicators and detect alerts.
paragraphs.p2: The analysis of data guides the controls.

inspection.title: Inspections
inspection.lead: An inspection is an in-depth on-site control.

paragraphs.p1: The inspection takes place in several stages: announcement, conduct, conclusions and follow-up.
paragraphs.p2: It gives rise to a report and recommendations.

paragraphs.p1: Reports, recommendations and corrections are subject to follow-up.
paragraphs.p2: Regular exchanges accompany the implementation of the corrections.

bullets.b1: The control reports.
bullets.b2: The recommendations.
bullets.b3: The corrections requested.

resultats.title: The results
resultats.lead: The results of the controls are used.

paragraphs.p1: The results may be published, monitored over time and integrated into the assessment of the situation of institutions.
paragraphs.p2: Transparency and proportionality guide this use.

hero.title: Sanctions and measures
hero.lead: In case of breach or fragility, graduated corrective measures may be taken. This page presents the principles.
hero.notice: No precise sanction is presented: the measures described are general principles awaiting the official framework.

comprendre.title: Understanding sanctions
comprendre.lead: Sanctions aim to put an end to breaches and to preserve stability.

paragraphs.p1: Sanctions and corrective measures are decisions taken against an institution in case of breach or fragility.
paragraphs.p2: They are graduated, proportionate and transparent.

definition.title: Definition
definition.text: The decisions in case of breach.

mesures.title: Corrective measures
mesures.lead: Several corrective measures may be taken.

paragraphs.p1: Corrective measures include the request for correction, preventive measures, restrictions and recovery plans.
paragraphs.p2: They aim to restore compliance and soundness.

gradation.title: The graduation of measures
gradation.lead: Measures are graduated according to severity.

paragraphs.p1: The graduation goes from the alert to the correction, then to the restriction, the suspension and, as a last resort, the withdrawal.
paragraphs.p2: Each stage corresponds to a degree of severity.

paragraphs.p1: The procedure includes the finding, the notification, the observation, the decision and the publication.
paragraphs.p2: It guarantees the rights of the defence.

integration.title: Prudential integration
integration.lead: The measures are part of prudential monitoring.

paragraphs.p1: Monitoring, recommendations, corrections and proportionality are part of the prudential approach.
paragraphs.p2: The objective is to durably restore compliance.

bullets.b1: The monitoring of measures.
bullets.b2: The recommendations.
bullets.b3: The corrections.

competence.title: The competence
competence.lead: The competence to sanction falls within the competent authority.

paragraphs.p1: In the Astorian model, financial supervision and sanctions fall within the independent mandate of the AMSF.
paragraphs.p2: The Central Bank acts within the framework of its own mandate.

competence.notice: The exact division of responsibilities will be the one provided for by Astorian law.

paragraphs.p1: The sanction may be published, entered in the register and open remedies.
paragraphs.p2: The consequences are proportionate to the severity of the breach.

hero.lead: The Central Bank of Astoria is committed to making its portal accessible, in accordance with the law of 8 July 2019. This declaration applies to the Central Bank of Astoria portal.
hero.notice: Last updated: 12 September 2026.

declaration.title: Our commitment
declaration.lead: The Central Bank of Astoria is committed to digital accessibility to make its portal usable by everyone, whatever the disability, device or connection.

paragraphs.p1: Digital accessibility means making content and services accessible to all, in particular to people with disabilities. It is an issue of equal opportunity and a public service commitment.
paragraphs.p2: The Central Bank of Astoria portal is built according to the general accessibility improvement framework (RGAA), to offer a consistent browsing experience to all visitors.

conformite.title: Compliance status
conformite.lead: The Central Bank of Astoria portal is partially compliant with the general accessibility improvement framework (RGAA), version 4.1, level AA.

bullets.b1: Keyboard and touch navigation is supported on all pages.
bullets.b2: Text content respects the contrast and legibility rules defined by the framework.
bullets.b3: Some advanced interactive components remain to be harmonised with the framework recommendations.

nonAccessibles.title: Non-accessible content
nonAccessibles.lead: Despite our vigilance, some content may present access difficulties. The following items are not yet accessible:

bullets.b1: Documents published in PDF format before the entry into force of this declaration.
bullets.b2: Some data charts and visualisations, for which a text alternative is planned.
bullets.b3: A few videos without a full transcript, currently being processed.

bullets.b3: Any procedure provided for by the law of 8 July 2019 and its implementing decree.

donnees.title: Data collected

bullets.b1: Browsing data: IP address, pages visited, browser and screen resolution, for audience measurement and security purposes.
bullets.b2: Platform identification data: login, email address and preferences, only for authenticated services.
bullets.b3: Declarative data: what you voluntarily enter in a portal form.

bullets.b3: Right to data portability of the data you have provided.

definition.title: What is a cookie?
definition.lead: A cookie is a small text file placed on your device when you visit a website.

paragraphs.p1: Cookies store information about your browsing (preferences, language, audience measurement) to improve your experience and understand how the portal is used.
paragraphs.p2: The portal only sets strictly necessary cookies and, subject to your consent, audience measurement cookies. No advertising cookies are used.

gestion.title: Manage your cookies
gestion.lead: You can accept or refuse non-essential cookies at any time, whichever method suits you best:

bullets.b1: From the cookie management banner, displayed on your first visit at the bottom left of the screen.
bullets.b2: By configuring your browser to refuse or delete cookies.
bullets.b3: By deleting the cookies already placed from your browser settings.

gestion.notice: Refusing audience measurement cookies does not affect how the portal works.
